marks.gloss_en: but one may put [spices] into a bowl or into a tureen
one may not place a vessel under the lamp to catch the oil in it
the hen lays on the dump where eggs are trodden: overturning a vessel on it is a common rescue, and that they permitted
the hen does not lay on a slope: a vessel beneath it is an uncommon rescue, and that they did not permit
one may not place a vessel under a hen to receive its egg
איתיביה אביי: והצלה שאינה מצויה לא התירו?! והתניא: a tevel barrel that broke on his roof -- he brings a vessel and sets it beneath!
בגולפי חדתי דשכיחי דפקעי -- new barrels, which commonly burst: a common rescue
if his barrel of tevel broke on his roof, he brings a vessel and places it beneath it
איתיביה: one may place a vessel under the lamp to receive sparks!
ניצוצות נמי שכיחי -- sparks are common too
one may place a vessel under the lamp to receive sparks
תא שמע, דתניא: רבי יהודה אומר לכל אילפסין הוא נותן, לכל הקדירות רותחות הוא נותן -- R' Yehuda permits the boiling pots themselves
R' Yehuda says: into all stew pots one puts [spices], into all boiling pots one puts [spices], except something containing vinegar or brine
והיינו דאמר רב נחמן: צריכא מילחא בישולא כבישרא דתורא -- that is what Rav Nachman said
Abaye (second version): 'salt is not like a spice' means that in a first vessel too it does not cook
אמר ליה אביי: תני רבי חייא, מלח אינה כתבלין -- R' Chiyya taught that salt is not like a spice (the same objection in both versions, 42b.4 and 42b.5)
Rav Yosef thought: salt is like a spice -- in a first vessel it cooks, in a second vessel it does not
R' Yehuda's clause refers to the first clause [the boiling pot], and is lenient
